semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The term 'interpretable feedforward neural network' implies a feed-forward structure, which is the same base architecture as the 'feed-forward neural network'. Both models are fundamentally about information flowing in one direction without any cycles or loops.
The plural form 'feed-forward neural networks' describes the same structural type of network as the singular 'feed-forward neural network' and would include 'interpretable' variations.

parent_models.justification: A 'neural network' is a broad category that encompasses various types of neural network architectures, including feed-forward types.
This is a more generalized term that includes all kinds of architectures such as feed-forward, recurrent, and others.
Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are a general class under which feed-forward and other types of networks fall. They describe any neural network that is used for computational purposes.
An 'interpretable feedforward neural network' typically means it is fully connected, where all neurons in one layer are connected to every neuron in the next layer.
Like its singular counterpart, it represents networks where every neuron is connected to every neuron in the succeeding layers.
